claim_1.claim: ELISA analysis of sera from 56 vaccinated individuals showed robust anti-spike IgG binding antibody responses after primary vaccination (day 0) and significantly boosted responses after secondary vaccination (day 21).

sources.quote: Primary vaccination induced binding antibody and neutralizing antibody responses in all but three individuals; these responses were boosted significantly after the secondary vaccination.
Fifty-six healthy volunteers were recruited for the study under informed consent.

comparison.finding: significantly boosted anti-spike IgG binding antibody responses after secondary vaccination

claim_2.claim: Neutralizing Antibody Titer Assay of sera from 56 vaccinated individuals showed neutralizing antibody responses against the wild-type SARS-CoV-2 strain after primary vaccination (day 0), with significantly boosted responses after secondary vaccination (day 21).

sources.quote: Primary vaccination induced binding antibody and neutralizing antibody responses in all but three individuals; these responses were boosted significantly after the secondary vaccination.
Fifty-six healthy volunteers were recruited for the study under informed consent.

comparison.finding: significantly boosted neutralizing antibody responses after secondary vaccination

claim_3.claim: CyTOF analysis of whole blood from 27 vaccinated individuals showed a significant increase in the frequency of inflammatory monocytes (CD14+ CD16+ monocytes) 2 days after primary vaccination (day 2) and a further increase 2 days after secondary vaccination (day 23).

sources.quote: The frequency of intermediate monocytes (CD14 + CD16 + monocytes) increased significantly two days after the primary vaccination, and was substantially higher two days after the secondary vaccination.
Fifty-six healthy volunteers were recruited for the study under informed consent.

comparison.finding: further increase in the frequency of inflammatory monocytes after secondary vaccination

claim_4.claim: Olink assay of plasma from 31 vaccinated individuals showed significant increases in IFNγ and CXCL10 levels on days 1 and 2 after primary vaccination (day 1-2), with further increases after secondary vaccination (day 21).

sources.quote: Of the 67 cytokines detected, the concentration of 2 cytokines (IFNγ and CXCL10) were increased significantly on days 1 and 2 after primary vaccination. Similar to our observations on intermediate monocytes and pSTAT1 and pSTAT3, the concentrations of these cytokines were increased even further after the secondary immunization.
Fifty-six healthy volunteers were recruited for the study under informed consent.

comparison.finding: significant increases in IFNγ and CXCL10 levels on days 1 and 2
further increases in IFNγ and CXCL10 levels after secondary vaccination

claim_5.claim: Bulk RNA-seq assay of whole blood from 31 vaccinated individuals showed a greater transcriptional response after secondary vaccination (day 21) compared to primary vaccination (day 0), with nearly a fourfold increase in differentially expressed genes at day 22 compared to day 1.

sources.quote: Secondary vaccination generated a greater transcriptional response, with nearly a fourfold increase of differentially expressed genes at day 22 as compared to day 1.
Fifty-six healthy volunteers were recruited for the study under informed consent.

comparison.finding: greater transcriptional response after secondary vaccination
nearly a fourfold increase in differentially expressed genes at day 22 compared to day 1

claim_6.claim: CITE-seq analysis of PBMCs from 6 vaccinated individuals revealed the emergence of a myeloid cell cluster (C8) enriched in interferon-response transcription factors one day after secondary vaccination (day 22), which was not present after primary vaccination (day 0).

sources.quote: Notably, cluster C8 (which expressed CD14, VCAN, CD1C, FCGR1A and CD274 mRNA or protein) emerged on day 22, one day after secondary vaccination.
Fifty-six healthy volunteers were recruited for the study under informed consent.

comparison.finding: emergence of a myeloid cell cluster (C8) enriched in interferon-response transcription factors after secondary vaccination
